top_temples.name: Mahadev Khola Dham
top_temples.location_note: Shillong; a roughly 150-year-old shrine discovered by a Subedar Major of the 8th Gurkha Rifles after a divine dream, major Maha Shivratri mela over three days.

top_temples.name: Matri Mandir (Ramna Kalibari)
top_temples.location_note: Shillong; one of the city's oldest and most architecturally distinctive temples, with nightly puja to Goddess Kali.

top_temples.name: Shankari Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Shillong; dedicated to a local deity believed to protect the city, especially attended during Durga Puja.

top_temples.name: Shree Shree Hanuman Mandir, Shillong
top_temples.location_note: Shillong; a hilltop temple offering views over the city.

top_temples.name: Gorkha Durga Temple, Shillong
top_temples.location_note: Shillong; a cultural and religious hub for the city's Gorkha community.

top_temples.name: Nartiang Durga Temple (Shri Maa Jayanti Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Nartiang village, about 60 km from Shillong in the Jaintia Hills near Jowai; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, over 500 years old, built by Jaintia King Dham Manik, marks where Sati's left thigh is believed to have fallen.

top_temples.name: Shiv Temple, Nartiang
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Nartiang temple precinct near Jowai as the Durga Temple; a distinct shrine sharing the same historic site.

top_temples.name: Tura Thakurbari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Lower Hawakhana, Tura; described as the spiritual heart of the West Garo Hills' Hindu community.

top_temples.name: Charantala Kali Temple
top_temples.location_note: Charantala, near Tura in the Garo Hills; believed by locals to protect the area, centre of the large annual Charantala Mela.
